docs.title: Share any terminal process with one link.
docs.intro: shell.online wraps a command in a local PTY, keeps it running on your machine, and exposes its live terminal through an interactive or server-enforced read-only URL.
cards: Run curl -fsSL https://shell.online/install | sh on macOS or Linux. The installer verifies SHA-256 before writing the binary and prints PATH instructions when needed.
Prefix an existing command: shell claude, shell codex, or shell python train.py. Omit the command for a fresh shell. The usable URL prints immediately.
Links are interactive by default. Add --read-only before the command when viewers should monitor without being able to send terminal input.
Add --e2ee to encrypt terminal input and output between the CLI and browsers. Use Docker when the same encrypted shell and URL should survive container restarts.

Use shell list to see local process uptime and the relay's independent online, reconnecting, expired, or unknown state. Use shell attach <ID> to take over locally and shell kill <ID> to stop one. Task exit always closes an ordinary share.

mobile.title: A real terminal, fitted to the device in your hand.
mobile.intro: A phone is not a smaller desktop. shell.online measures the visual viewport, accounts for the on-screen keyboard, and resizes the PTY—not merely its CSS box.
cards: One connected viewer owns the shared PTY size at a time. Active input can transfer ownership; a local attachment takes priority. Other viewers never make the TUI jump.
Single-finger gestures scroll normal terminal history. When an application enables mouse tracking or its alternate screen, the same gesture is translated into terminal wheel input.
The terminal follows visualViewport changes through keyboard open, dismiss, rotation, and browser chrome movement. Ctrl-C, Ctrl-W, selection-copy, and binary terminal replies have dedicated paths.
Paste input is split into Worker-safe 16 KiB frames and waits for WebSocket backpressure. A browser cannot turn one large paste into an unbounded memory queue.

reliability.title: The link can disappear. Your process should not.
reliability.intro: The PTY and command live on your machine. Relay and browser failures are treated as recoverable display failures, never as permission to terminate local work.
cards: The CLI and browser reconnect with bounded backoff. A temporary network failure does not stop the process, and disconnected ordinary sessions retain a 15-minute relay grace window.
A bounded local ring buffer restores new or returning viewers. If live output outruns either network or rendering, shell.online drops stale display work and sends one authoritative screen snapshot.
PTY reads never wait indefinitely for Cloudflare. WebSocket writes time out, queues are bounded, frames have size and traffic limits, and high-output processes keep running locally.

The URL prints immediately. shell list distinguishes local process liveness from relay status, including expired links and inconclusive network checks; shell attach rejoins locally and shell kill stops the process. Ordinary shares and server state disappear when the task exits.

security.title: Know exactly what the link grants—and what the relay sees.
security.intro: Ordinary sessions use encrypted transport and include Cloudflare in the content trust boundary. Optional --e2ee sessions encrypt terminal payloads on the CLI and browser. Both modes have explicit limits.
cards: The URL is a bearer capability
Anyone holding an interactive URL can view and type with the wrapped process’s operating-system permissions. Share it only with intended collaborators and run with least privilege.
With --read-only, browser input is rejected by the Worker. DevTools or handcrafted WebSocket frames cannot turn the link into an interactive session.

Without --e2ee, HTTPS/WSS encrypts each hop but terminal bytes pass through Cloudflare in memory. With --e2ee, Cloudflare routes authenticated ciphertext while frame type, size, timing, IP, and session metadata remain visible.
Cloudflare does not persist terminal contents. The CLI holds only a bounded in-memory replay buffer while the process is alive; ordinary task exit deletes the session state and closes every socket.

e2ee.title: Terminal contents only the machine and its browsers can read.
e2ee.intro: Add --e2ee to encrypt every terminal payload with AES-256-GCM before it enters the relay. Keys are generated locally, URL fragments never reach Cloudflare, and password derivation happens on-device.
cards: shell --e2ee <command> generates a fresh 256-bit key and puts it after #key= in the share URL. Browsers import that fragment locally; browsers never send URL fragments in HTTP or WebSocket requests.
Set SHELL_ONLINE_E2EE_PASSWORD before starting the CLI. The URL contains only a random salt, and the browser derives the same key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 after the recipient enters the password.

Terminal input, output, snapshots, resizes, and latency probes are authenticated ciphertext. Cloudflare can still see connection IPs, timing, encrypted sizes, frame opcodes, access mode, labels, and lifecycle metadata.

E2EE cannot hide traffic shape or prevent the relay from dropping, delaying, or replaying a valid encrypted frame. A lost random-key URL or Docker password cannot be recovered. Anyone with the complete URL—or password plus salted URL—can decrypt.

cli.title: Every command and option, in one place.
cli.intro: The shell CLI starts shares, reports their real relay state, attaches to local PTYs, and stops them. Run shell help reference to keep this complete reference available in the terminal too.
cards: Wrap a command in a local PTY, print its browser URL, and run it in the background. With no command, shell starts $SHELL or /bin/sh. Put -- before the command when argument boundaries are ambiguous.
Share a command in the background.
Options apply when a new share is created. Access and encryption modes cannot be weakened after creation.
Create an immutable view-only link; the relay rejects browser input.
Encrypt terminal frames between CLI and browser.
Reuse one stable E2EE identity and URL; requires --e2ee.
Mirror and control the process in the launching terminal.
Add an earlier deadline; task exit remains the maximum lifetime.
Emit the new-session event as JSON on stderr.
Print the CLI version and exit.

List locally managed processes and independently check the relay. Table states are online, starting, reconnecting, expired, and unknown; unknown means the check was inconclusive, not that the link died.
Print ID, uptime, relay, closing rule, access, command, and URL.
Print a JSON array on stdout with raw relay_status values: connected, waiting, disconnected, expired, or unknown.
Attach to an existing local PTY without disabling browser access. IDs may be complete or unambiguous prefixes of at least six characters. Local input and resulting output remain visible online.
Detach while leaving the process and share running.
Legacy detach alternative; Ctrl-Z is not detach.
Stopping sends termination to the wrapped process and closes its browser session. Completed tasks already close themselves automatically.
Stop one session by full ID or unambiguous prefix.

Guided help is built into the executable, including this full reference. Command aliases do not change behavior.
Show the guided workflow and common options.
Topics: start, attach, list, kill, reference.
Print the complete built-in CLI reference.
Help-topic aliases for start; starting a process remains shell <command>.
A share always closes when its task exits. --auto-close can only add an earlier deadline. Bare --auto-close means task-bound closure, which is already the default.
Relative units: ms, s, m, h, d, w, mo, and y.

Normal starts print the share URL and lifecycle details. Structured starts emit one JSON event on stderr so the wrapped process keeps stdout. Background start returns after the share is ready; foreground mode returns the wrapped process status.

docker.title: One encrypted shell and one stable link across restarts.
docker.intro: The Docker client keeps its workspace, host credential, E2EE key, and share identity in named volumes. Restart the container and the same browser URL reconnects to the new PTY.
cards: Pull ghcr.io/teoslayer/shell.online:0.6.2 or run docker compose up --build -d, then docker compose logs shell-online. The tagged amd64/arm64 image includes an SBOM and build provenance.
shell-online-state stores the host credential, share identity, and E2EE material. shell-online-workspace stores the container workspace. Treat the state volume and its backups as secrets.

The container reconnects the same relay identity and URL after a restart. Connected browser pages remain open and report offline until the host returns. An unused offline identity expires from the relay after 30 days but can be revived from its state volume.

This image is a persistent client for the hosted shell.online relay, not a self-hosted relay. It does not make the container immortal, publish ports, or recover a deleted volume or forgotten password.
